changes.softwareVerification: Protocol/action scope verified: four zones, exact ApplyLeds order/waits, second LED set, fixed speed, OXP classic 1000, brightness-0 off and exact preset set through the existing helper. Owner/lifecycle software boundaries are now implemented in the same total-library owner: a generation-specific revocation event plus an authoritative named handoff record; admission and busy decision in one short state transaction without holding the input/stop owner mutex across pending-write waits; write and bind gated for admission, lease and retiring states; the helper matches the current generation token, exact endpoint and fresh owner heartbeat before open/first write and between wait slices; a timeout retains retiring/pending-IO debt until the exact helper process is signaled and the pending write returns; only the matching token may release and a late receipt cannot free a newer owner. When the post-termination wait is still unsignaled, the exact child process handle and its token are retained; helper/application flags remain debt markers and owner-tick, next-admission and stop settlement stay closed until that handle is observed signaled, then exactly one retirement clears the debt. An unrelated or late child cannot retire a newer lease. Each admission also carries a unique admission number in the handoff token and event name, so two sequential leases on the same unchanged device never share a token or event; the old token cannot rejoin or free the newer lease. The effective request deadline and owning-lease revocation are linked into admission, device open, the write sequence and its in-flight IO; the production ExecuteOxp3LightingWith path is exercised with a held pending write, and both owner revocation and request expiry cancel it. The complete production ymccLightSetterApply parent is executed with real admission, command construction, anonymous-pipe spawn, production wait, exact-child debt/lease transition, bounded reads, JSON identity/catalog/operation checks and the receipt gate: an owned inert software helper yields the accepted receipt, spawn failure, timeout with observed signaled return, output truncation, read error, read timeout, no-JSON, nonzero exit, child-not-ok and wrong identity/catalog/operation branches. A normal full-rights timeout shows the observed signaled return; a second complete-parent timeout hands the parent a controlled process handle without PROCESS_TERMINATE at the harness spawn terminal, so TerminateProcess fails access-denied and the production parent retains the actual unsignaled child/token/handle; with input writePending=false, tick, admission, write and rebind stay closed, one settlement follows the actual return, re-admission succeeds and the old token is rejected. The actual Oxp3WindowsHidTransport Write path reaches an explicit issued barrier; direct owned CancelIoEx cancels the pending OS write and returns true, while Program owner and deadline cancellation complete the pending write with the terminal CancelIoEx outcome recorded (ERROR_NOT_FOUND after the runtime already canceled), handle cleanup and zero later ordinary writes. Recorded CancelIoEx outcomes are [0] for the direct owned cancel and [1168] for each Program path; the managed transport also records the same IO as incomplete at issue, token-uncancelled at issue and cancelled-while-incomplete for both Program paths; the request deadline is 1500 ms, before the 2000 ms transport and owner-heartbeat boundaries, and the per-generation event is created in the controlled scenario. The complete parent test references the existing fixed device-core runtime read-only (HandheldCompanion.dll 08a386607a0e5e72c5fcaa98d3a6c0b3b256eb0fca7d6547f6f124c1f1f33583) and records its runtime.json identity; no synthetic DLL or copied runtime is created.
